Image 1 shows the real Spraymax bottle: a low-light photo of its front, and close-ups of its pump from the side and from the front. Use Image 1 only for the bottle's shape, proportions, plastic, ribbed collar, pump head, nozzle and clear overcap. Image 2 is the bottle's complete flat label artwork. Use Image 2 only for the label print, wrapped once around the body: its centre panel, with the indigo Spraymax wordmark running top to bottom, the line Instant Hair Volume & Texture and the dark navy ocean-wave band, faces the front, and the small-text panels wrap round the sides and back. Define the bottle from Image 1 wearing the label from Image 2 as <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> is identical in every shot, always with its clear overcap on.

Product truth: <Subject 1> is a slim 100 ml bottle about 14 cm tall, about four times as tall as it is wide, roughly the length of a hand, with a rounded shoulder, made of milky, slightly grey-white semi-matte plastic with a soft sheen and fine real surface texture; a matte white, finely ribbed collar; a small matte white pump head; a clear, lightly frosted overcap. It is a sealed, light plastic bottle: in water it sinks slowly and tumbles gently, and on sand or rock it lies naturally on its side.

A 12-second vertical luxury film for Spraymax Himalayan sea salt hair spray in the spirit of a high-end men's fragrance campaign at sea: at sunset a lone man dives from a sea cliff, the bottle drops into the ocean and sinks through shafts of light to a shipwreck on the sea floor, then lies washed up on the rocks in the last light. Ten hard-cut shots in real locations, each with one deliberate camera move.

Hard cuts only throughout: every shot is a completely separate camera setup. No transitions, no dissolves, no wipes, no fades, no morphing, no motion carrying across a cut.

Real photography, inherited by every shot: filmed on an ARRI Alexa 35 with cinema lenses, the aerial shot from a cinema drone, the underwater shots in an underwater housing in clear open sea, the slow-motion shots on a Phantom high-speed camera at 1000 frames per second. Real places and real physics: a dark volcanic sea cliff, the open ocean at sunset, a real wooden shipwreck on white sand, real fish, sea grass, sand and foam, the bottle physically dropped into the water at its true size. Water behaves exactly as in life: bubbles rise and wobble, light rays shimmer, sand puffs and settles. Natural film grain, gentle lens falloff; no beauty smoothing, no plastic sheen, no over-sharpening, no haze over the whole frame.

Global look: sunset, vertical 9:16. Above the water, a low sun on the horizon, a warm orange-gold sky and a dark sea, everything else in silhouette. Below the water, deep ocean blue and teal, sunlight falling in shafts from a glowing surface. The man is only ever a dark silhouette or seen from behind; his face is never visible. Mostly dark negative space; the bottle is small in wide shots and fills the frame only in its close-ups.

Never render: any face; any person other than the lone man in silhouette at 00:00.0 and 00:01.2; the bottle standing upright on sand or rock as if posed in a studio; the bottle larger than a hand, or hovering above the ground; a warped, bent, melting or resized bottle; the overcap off; liquid leaking from the bottle; misspelled, mirrored or duplicated label text; a visible light fixture of any kind; lens flares; logos on clothing; any text other than the bottle's own label; captions or watermarks; purple or violet light.

[00:00.0] Wide aerial at sunset. A lone man stands at the edge of a dark volcanic sea cliff high above the ocean, a small black silhouette against the low sun and the orange sky, the sea glittering below. The drone drifts slowly toward him.

[00:01.2] From below and behind, Phantom slow motion: the man dives off the cliff edge into the sea, his body a dark silhouette arcing against the glowing orange sky, his face never visible. Camera holds still.

[00:02.2] Underwater, looking up at the glowing sunset surface. <Subject 1> plunges in from above, punching a cavity of air into the water and trailing a burst of silver bubbles, then slows and begins to sink, tumbling gently, shafts of sunlight around it. Camera holds still, slightly below.

[00:03.6] Underwater close-up. <Subject 1> sinks slowly past the lens, front label toward the camera, tiny bubbles clinging to the clear overcap and the label, the indigo wordmark sharp, blue water behind. Camera drifts down with it.

[00:04.6] The sea floor, deep blue and teal: the broken wooden hull of an old shipwreck lies on white sand, ribs of timber open to the water, shafts of light falling through, small fish drifting, and high above it the small white shape of <Subject 1> sinking toward the sand. Camera drifts slowly forward.

[00:05.8] Close to the sand beside the wreck's broken timbers. <Subject 1> lands softly and settles naturally on its side, raising a small puff of sand that drifts and settles, sea grass swaying beside it, caustic light rippling over the label. Camera pushes in slowly.

[00:07.0] A school of small silver fish turns as one above the wreck, flashing in the shafts of sunset light falling from the surface. Camera holds still, looking up.

[00:07.9] Above water at sunset: a wave breaks over dark volcanic rocks at the shoreline, the spray backlit gold by the low sun, Phantom slow motion. Camera holds still.

[00:08.9] Close-up at the waterline: <Subject 1> lies naturally on its side on wet black rocks, washed up, front label facing up; a wave washes over it and draws back, leaving foam fizzing around it and water beading on the plastic. Camera holds still.

[00:10.0] Hero packshot at sunset. <Subject 1> lies on its side on the wet dark rocks, front label to camera, catching the last warm light of the sun on the horizon behind it, the sea soft and glowing, the upper half of the frame open sky. Camera pushes in very slowly, almost imperceptibly.

Throughout: <Subject 1> keeps its exact shape, size, label and colours from Images 1 and 2, the label sharp and correctly spelled; no new reflections. Keep it subtitle-free, with no captions and no watermark. No other logos. No music and no voices.
